acceptance.criterion_verbatim: A FIRST-VISIT VIEWER WITH NO STORED SELECTION LANDS ON INT. Verified on a CLEARED profile (or a fresh/private one), and the report STATES the profile state.
acceptance.denominator: 1 cleared-profile render at 1440x900 fullPage, READ; 5 model books in the selector.
acceptance.output_evidence: PROFILE STATE: CLEARED -- ui-smoke launches with no userDataDir and no storageState, so localStorage is empty by construction. RENDERED READ: the Portfolio Composition selector shows INT active (green). The pre-change baseline render at the same width and the same cleared state shows UST active (orange), so the two are DISCRIMINATING rather than merely consistent. PROFILE-STATE CONTROL: AC1 therefore ran on a CLEARED profile, which is the only state in which this change is observable at all. 3.0.0_SA_CVO~Z named the mirror hazard (msg 12762): a viewer whose storage already holds INT sees INT whether or not the fix landed, and that FALSE PASS is silent. A warm browser cannot fail this test, so it cannot pass it either.

acceptance.criterion_verbatim: MODEL_BOOKS ORDER IS UNCHANGED. bookSet.ts:78 still reads ['UST','ST','INT','LT','ULT']. Show the array is byte-identical.
acceptance.denominator: 1 line, sha256 compared before and after, plus a write-time assertion in the patch script.
acceptance.output_evidence: sha256 of the MODEL_BOOKS line: e472015d09b56fc1 BEFORE and e472015d09b56fc1 AFTER -- byte-identical, re-checked after every exercise including the AC4 mutant. The patch script additionally ASSERTS the literal line is present at write time and aborts otherwise, so a reorder could not have been committed silently. WHY IT MATTERS: the order is an INDEX CONTRACT -- customBlend builds each row's values by mapping over the resolved set in that order, so a reorder misaligns every blended cell while columns still sum to something plausible. The failure would be SILENT.

acceptance.criterion_verbatim: THE CARRIES-ROWS CONDITION SURVIVES. If INT holds no rows in a given mode, the viewer must NOT land on an empty book. Name what happens in that case.
acceptance.denominator: 1 exercised render with the preference pointed at a declared shell; 4 ETF books, 1 of them a shell.
acceptance.output_evidence: WHAT HAPPENS, NAMED: the preference is gated on the same carriesRows predicate the existing rule uses, so a shell preference is REFUSED and control falls through to books.find(carriesRows), then books[0]. EXERCISED, not argued: with the preference pointed at IDVZ (a declared shell) the page landed on DIVZ, the first book carrying rows. Without the gate it would have opened on the shell's 'Book-level metrics only' state. Reverted immediately; the filed commit reads 'INT'. SECOND GUARD: books.includes(PREFERRED_DEFAULT_BOOK) scopes the preference to families that HAVE the book -- ETF and satellite sets do not contain INT and fall through untouched, so this is data-driven rather than mode-driven and no future mode can inherit it.
